Churyumov S.I., "Smile of the Cheshire Cat": 

  

Part of Preface, Table of Contents, summaries of Chapters 1 and 2, Chapters 3 to 7. (Remaining chapters 8 to 20 from the original source were write protected and could not be translated.)

**From Preface:**

  

The Cheshire Cat from Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland had the amazing ability to appear and disappear in parts. When he appeared, his smile was the first to appear, and when he disappeared, it was the last to disappear.

  

On the one hand, the Cheshire Cat's smile is perceived as something really tangible and understandable, quite sensory, but on the other hand, there is some kind of mystical elusiveness and independence in it. Similarly, there are many socionic concepts - information aspects (IA), socionic functions (SF) and the types of information metabolism (TIMs) themselves - we do not doubt their reality, we know how to work with them, we have learned to recognize and identify them with a certain degree of reliability and consensus, we see some of their signs and manifestations (first-order factors), but they are not directly, that is, sensorily, recorded, remaining factors of the second, third and higher orders. It is becoming increasingly clear that these concepts require deep methodological analysis, and that they take us to the edge beyond which rational human intellect becomes powerless.

**Table of Contents:**

Chapter 1:

An overview of existing and new hypotheses on the nature of the mental substrate are given, and clarifications are made to Ausra's hypothesis on the possible connection between energy meridians and mental functions.

Chapter 2:

The basic socionic problem of information metabolism is considered and, as a hypothetical construct, a scheme of combinatorial synthesis of information aspects is proposed, when they are expressed through the basic for modern science ultimate abstractions of matter, energy and information. Here we propose an objective, i.e. independent of the perceiving subject, understanding of information as a code of the form of an object, since the code of the form of arbitrary objects is formed and is present in any physical fields according to the corresponding laws of nature.

Chapter 3:

The problem of mental functions, their semantics, their possible generalization is considered and a hypothesis of their origin in the process of evolution of the human type of psyche is proposed.

Chapter 4:

The problem of modeling the human psyche is considered from a new angle and three models are proposed that in no way deny model "A” but are its developments.

Chapter 5:

Formulates and examines the problem of existence, uniqueness and diversity within TIM in connection with the assessment of psychological characteristics of a specific individual and considering that TIM is the main object of socionics.

Chapter 6:

Examines the problem of differentiating features in psychology in general and in socionics in particular.

Chapter 7:

Substantiates for the first time in socionic research the idea of ​​socionics as a periodic system of information metabolism types and introduces the concept of an elementary object in psychology and informatics.

  

Not translated due to copyright  protections of source material:

  

Chapter 8:

Formulates and examines the problem of the relationship between the concepts of type and character in relation to socionics.

Chapter 9:

Examines the problem of geometric and symbolic configurations in socionics, as well as the problem of digital coding of TIM, and the concept of symbolic spaces. A preliminary review of thirty-five correct (Reinin) fours is also provided.

Chapter 10:

Discusses the problem of diagnosing TIM.

Chapter 11:

Examines the problem of describing TIM.

Chapter 12:

Based on the previously proposed by the author principle of duality of the socionic type and intertype relationship, two models of intertype relationship are proposed, which makes it possible to constructively describe socionic relationships.

Chapter 13:

The hypothesis of the universality of the socionic type in relation to any subjects and objects is considered, which is still ambiguously perceived among socionics theorists.

Chapter 14:

Examines the problem of the origin of typological differentiation within the species homo sapiens, which requires deep psychological and anthropological research. It is hoped that posing this problem in a socionic key will attract the attention of all interested specialists.

Chapter 15:

Examines the problem of the relationship between socionics and psychology and makes several assumptions about the possibility of solving the problem of the theoretical substantiation of psychology.

Chapter 16:

Compares the theoretical positions of Freud, Jung, Ausra, and other scientists regarding personality structure.

Chapter 17:

Examines the relationship between socionics and philosophy.

Chapter 18:

Examines the eternal theme associated with the concepts of sex and social hypocrisy in their connection with socionics.

Chapter 19:

Provides a preliminary and far from complete review of the methodological complexes of leading socionics, and presents some blunders, myths and artifacts that have accumulated in socionics over the short century of its existence.

Chapter 20:

Examines the methodological potential of socionics as a research tool in other humanitarian and not necessarily humanitarian disciplines.

Appendices:

Present materials of various natures, including personal, reference and discussion.

**Directly related to Socionics excerpts from Chapters 1 and 2**

  

Se:  Reality, a real object in all the fullness of its manifestations.

Fe:  A state, an energetic characteristic of an object.

Te:  Transformation, the process of transforming some objects into others.

Ne:  Potential, potential capabilities of an object.

Si:  Value, aesthetic, and consumer parameters of an object.

Fi:   Integrity, relation.

Ti:   Space, parameters of the form and position of an object.

Ni:  Time, the course of a process, proceduralist.

  

**Se vs Si** 

Ausra associated Se with form, the appearance of objects, wealth, force pressure.  Si with comfort, aesthetic attitude to life, and usefulness.

But spatial relationships, for example, closer, farther, big, small, and others, are not associated with Si.

  

**Te:** 

A process of the emergence of new objects based on the transformation of previously existing ones. And even if the transformed object can be considered the same in several formal characteristics, then at the level of extreme generalizations any quantitative changes can be considered as the emergence of a new quality. And in this case the transformed object can be considered as new. In this archetype the internal turns into the external. This archetype at the level of functional semantics can be considered as the technological activity of the subject.

  

**Si:**

  

A generalized image of reality from the point of view of its ultimate importance for the subject.

  

**Fi:**

  

An integrity. A relation is a pair effect.  Two objects are in a certain relation if their behavior and/or state causally depend on their interaction.  Behavior is the trajectory of an object in the space of its external parameters. State is the trajectory of an object in the space of its internal parameters.

  

**Ti and Ni:**

  

Correlate with the concepts of space and time.

  

  

**Matter-space (External: sensorics-logic)  &  Energy-time (Internal: ethics-intuition)**

  

Relate to each other as external and internal varieties of the same essence.

  

Matter-space:

No space separate from matter exists; space completely coincides with the contours of matter. Space is an abstraction associated with matter. Space is associated with a large empty place in which material objects are placed - something like a closet filled with things.  But space is only an introverted image of matter. This is why the abstraction of space is convenient to use to describe material objects.

  

Energy-time:

Similar reasoning applies.  There is no flow of time separate from the world. Time is an image of energy processes.

**Information aspect - Physical element correlations**

  

Sensorics - fire - time

Intuition - air - space

Emotionality - water - energy

Logic - earth - matter.

  

1) Why is fire time?  Because in the flame of fire everything burns, and time, turns out to be stronger than all. Everything passes, and nothing remains. Time heals everything.

  

2) Why is sensorics fire?  Because sensorics is active and connected with consumption, and fire cannot exist if it is not given fuel.

  

3) Why is air space?   Because air fills everything, penetrates everywhere and is almost unnoticeable. Therefore, it can be compared with intuition, because intuition penetrates everywhere, and there are no barriers to it, and it is also almost elusive.

  

4) Why is earth matter?   Because it is solid. 

  

5) Why is logic earth?   Because logic is “iron”. Logic consists of very strict formal rules that no one can violate without losing their meaning. If we compare logic with earth, then it will be natural to compare thinking with it. The same archetype is behind logic and thinking. The difference is only in the verbal-conceptual design.

  

6) Why is emotionality water?   Because emotionality, like water, is very plastic. It can acquire various modalities and shades: babbling like a gentle stream, carrying away with a powerful current, breaking ships against a wave, as if against a knee, or smashing them against rocks. And why is water energy? It is easy to understand if you stand on the seashore during a storm. But the sea is not always raging. So, energy can be potential, when you will not even suspect its existence.  But there are very sensitive people who feel hidden, unmanifested energy very well.

**Extroverted (materialized)**

Se: Real objects, Reality:

Exerts a forceful impact on its environment, on other objects, and really asserts its presence and existence.  Acts as a subject of observable changes in the environment. 

  

Fe: State of the object, level of energy activity

Active energy processes associated with the object and indicating its current state.

  

Te: Process of object transformation (real and abstract)

Performs work, manipulating objects, and technology.   Since technology leads to a real transformative change in the form of new objects.

  

Ne: Potential capabilities of the object:

Understanding of the laws of real, material, external objects, penetration into its essence, comprehension of the laws of its existence and functioning.  Its hidden capabilities.

  

**Introverted (immaterial)**

  

 Si: parameters of the object’s form

Values usefulness, aesthetics, practicality, well-being and, in general, any parameters of an object that are significant for the consumer, which can also be understood as value.

Characterized by the absence or minimum of a material component, since these are abstract concepts expressing the subject's attitude to what he consumes.

The information is external, that is real entities form, and not its description. Here the real object itself is assessed, its specific form, and we are dealing here with the first-signal perception of a material situation, the expected result, the state of the organism, the object of art, and the like. Here one could object that, for example, a work of art is a code of some life situation, and a code is an introverted form of existence. However, works of art in themselves, as an object of consumption, are quite material, since their carrier is always specific consumable materials - paints, sounds, paper, canvas, film, etc. But here there is a more subtle point related to the fact that works of art also have more ephemeral material, specific to each type of art. For example, in painting it is a line, color and spot. And although the line, color and spot, as objects of perception, despite the fact that their substrate is a concrete substance, are immaterial, but their form itself exists in reality, and is not encoded, as, for example, in a review or a critical article.

  

Fi: Relationship of the object’s parts

Integrity, attitude. Unlike emotionalization, which represents something brought out, attitude is encoded emotions, emotionality in an introverted form, that is, an ideal object…..there is an energetic connection between the objects in the relationship….in the case of a relationship the energetic component may be imperceptible. Can we say in this case that the energy of feelings is retained in a potential form and thus introverted?  The relation is always certain actions, certain behavior….

As for the information component of the relation, it is in an introverted form, since the system of relations is an information code of communication, and the code transfers us from materialized situations and objects to non-materialized ones. With the help of relations, certain meanings are encoded, the denotates of which are outside the relations and to which the relations point.  We can also talk about the information field of relations.

  

Ti:  Parameters of the object’s position in space

Potential energy and extroverted form, or simply form….  This deductive formula as thinking, we can conclude that introverted thinking is immaterial, that is, it does not operate with material objects, as is the case with extroverted thinking - technology, but with codes, images of these objects.

The energy of objects of thinking is in an introverted form, since these objects themselves are still only being "made", they represent a project of a future materialized something, to which only then can energy sources be connected and brought into active action. Here we should not be misled by the fact that thought objects can be thought of as actively acting, since the thought object in this case is the totality of the object and its action.

As for the information component of thinking, in this process it has its own form, immanent to it, therefore, although thinking itself as an introverted transformation of reality is immaterial, its form, as adequate to its essence, should be recognized as external.

In introverted thinking, matter is introverted, or….. is in a potential form. The same, as was done above, can be said about energy. But the form in thinking is external – this is the form of equations, descriptions, theories, etc., which here themselves are not in a coded form, but are presented in an adequate reality corresponding to them.

The same deductive formula can also be interpreted as space, since it is immaterial, passive in terms of energy, but has a real, manifested form. This form can be called empty or absolute, but it is real, directly embodied as an empty container and can be filled with any content.

The identity of deductive formulas of thinking and space is heuristic and significant. Due to this identity, thinking can be called the space of ideal transformation of reality. This is the space of modeling the subject's environment. Here modeling is a symbolic, informational imitation of the real life of the subject. In addition, due to such symbolic identity, thinking can be defined as modeling spatial forms and spatial relations, and one can even insist that there is nothing else in it. Here one may object – can’t we think, for example, emotional forms? To this one can answer that an emotional form is also a certain object localized in conceptual space.

At least, this is how emotional forms look from the point of view of thinking, which gravitates toward objectivity.

Thinking as a reflection, a symbolic reproduction of reality gravitates toward objectivity. Objectivity here can be understood as a reproduction of the life situation of the subject of thinking, as close as possible to the real state of affairs. For the subject, this is essential since such thinking should contribute to his survival. Fantastic thinking, disconnected from reality, represent two different forms of non-objective thinking. The first is a pathological case, and the second can perform various functions, which can include, for example, play, training, and psychological defense.

Ni: Temporal parameters of the object

Awareness of the subject's inner world.

Corresponds to time, which can be considered as pure potentiality, where everything has already been or will be - there will be substance, there will be energy and there will be form. The negativity of time, expressed by three minuses in its deductive formula, is also heuristic here.

  

**4 Information processes arising between subject (S) and object (O) communicants:**

**1) SO: Thinking** (Information is transferred from the subject to the object.)

The subject actively influences the object. Transforming, changing, and generating new objects.

In human practice, this active and transformative behavior is associated with:

-Te: Power, work, technology.

-Ti:  Objective definitions of characteristics of things, construction of theories, substantiation and proof, processing, and issuance of information.

**2) OS: Sensorics** (Information is transferred from the object to the subject.)

Passive perception of sensory flow.

Physical objects are the source of light, sound, and gravity waves that carry signals of information to the subject.

Associated with the passive influence of the object on the knower.

As a result of such influence, the world forces a person to change, and it is necessary to become passive and tune in to the information flow coming from the object.

**3) SS: Ethics** (Information flows between 2 subjects.)

One subject enters a relationship with another subject and experiences or evokes certain emotions in the other.  Emotions in this case are primary, and relationships, being the information code of an emotional reaction, are secondary.

Note:

It is easy to fall into a misconception that interactions between people are no different in its structure from the SO and OS situations. However, this is demonstrated to be false by comparing a mirror reflecting a random object with a mirror reflecting another mirror. Showing a person dealing with a thing is fundamentally different from dealing with another person.

An SS situation perceived as an SO situation results in inhumanely treating another person as a thing.

The temptation to perceive the SS situation as OS leads to people considering other people to be the same as themselves, and therefore, when faced with misunderstanding, they are surprised and indignant, and then proceed to impose their opinion and will on the other.

The SS situation - the transfer of information from subject to subject - is most important and the most difficult for a person, since here the subject interacts with the subject and, thus, ultimately, with himself.

**4) OO: Intuition** (Information is transferred from object to object)

Associated with the existence of an object independent of the subject, as well as with the objective existence of the subject.  

The identification of the subject with the object is quite consistent with socionic intuition.  Which involves information interactions between objects in a system of natural laws formulated as information imperatives.   Perceived by the subject as universal principles reflected in the harmony observed in nature.

To participate in this intuitive process the subject must merge with the object, enter into the system of objective relations and act not from egoistic or momentary motives, but on making the only correct decision that increases the harmony of the world.  He must act as an object.

V.D. Ermak

EGO and ID blocks: Executive

SUPEREGO and SUPERID: Controlling

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The four mental or psychic functions identified by Jung:

1) Intuitive comprehension; 2) sensory recognition; 3) logical thinking; and 4) emotional evaluation.

Jung’s model: Leading function, 2 less developed auxiliary functions, inferior function. 

Jung, apparently, did not assume that these two middle processes are also ordered by level of awareness.

Ausra presented the "J" model in a linear sequence. Function 1 is the most developed and conscious, function 4 is the most infantile, and function 2 and 3 are located between them in descending order according to the degree of awareness and development.

Ausra suggested that 4 mental functions are associated with bodily, or vital, processes. The products of the 4 vital functions are almost not consciously realized, being automatic responses of the body systems to mental processes.

-------------------------------------------------

FIELDS:

1. Ne: Primary meanings, or archetypes.

2. Ni: Internal meanings.

3. Se:  Reality.  Meanings and elements related to the objective world.

4. Si:  Mental (Translator’s note: does he mean body??)

5. Fi:  Intertype relations.

6. Fe: Emotional states.

7. Ti:  Differentiates features in structures of objects.

8. Te:  Means of material transformation. Technological. 

--------------------------------------

Ti includes speech, language and the process of verbal communication. An exit into space as an introverted image of the environment.  Primarily into communicative space.

Te is production activity, the ideal or material product of which is issued into the environment, becoming a source of resources for others and oneself.

Fi is attitude (towards people), including critical.

Si is a positive reserve necessary for a living being to survive. Expendable resources in need of replenishment, not expected to be covered by internal capabilities.

----------------------------------------

Fe vs Fi:

The emotional (Fe) reaction is predominantly directed outward, and therefore extroverted, while the attitude (aka Fi), primarily has an internal signal and can therefore be considered an introverted product.

Se vs Si:

Se: Negative pressure of the environment, a threatening impact, painful, dangerous, incompatible with life. 

Si: Positive impact of the environment, resource support, pleasant, useful.

Ausra adapted the thermodynamic cycle of an internal combustion engine to describe 4 information-energy cycles.  2 Potential cycles followed by 2 kinetic (program) cycles.

THERMODYNAMIC CYCLES: ILE

**1) Potential:** 

1/1 Se Role (Adaptive-load): 

Structures effort.  Perceives and adapts to the force pressure of the environment.  Responds to the impact of environmental loads. Protection and aggression, in case of extreme impact of the environment.

 1/2 Si Suggestive (Expectation-resource):

Structures consumption. Readiness to accept a resource.  Expects and accumulates potential material reserves.  

**2) Potential:**

2/1 Fi PoLR (Conservative-critical):  

Structures relations.  Forms a critical attitude to (Se) information pressure.  Meticulously selects from the neutral objectively real (Se) environment. 

2/2 Fe Mobilizing (Motivational-mobilization):   

Structures assessment.  Emotional reaction to the received resource.  Requests, vectors, hooks the psyche to transform potential material resource information into an imperative further kinetic processing.

**3) Kinetic (Program):**

3/1 Ne Base (Program-potential): 

Structures knowledge.  Internally models material features found in the external environment. Programs potential possibilities.

3/2 Ni Ignoring (Imperative-temporal): 

Structures time.  Concentrates on implementing program.

**4) Kinetic (Program):**

4/1 Ti Creative (Communicative-probing): 

Structures information.  Communicates, probes the environment.

4/2 Te Demonstrative (Implementation-technological): 

Structures the environment.  Physically labors and implements the final product that adequately ensures further survival.  Obtains product.

-------------------------------------------

ASPECT EXAMPLES & DESCRIPTIONS

**1/1 Adaptive-load (Role):**

Examples:

The decisive forceful resistance that can be provided by ILE and IEE, when there is a need to resist aggression, although on average aggressiveness is not characteristic of them.

SLE and SEE, being potentially aggressive, in case of necessity to resist pressure, exceeding their physical capabilities, resort to technical means and techniques, possessing increased Ne potential capabilities.

EII, being highly humane, in case of necessity to resist environmental pressure, resort to Ti sophisticated argumentation and devotes a lot of time to increasing their own erudition.

**1/2 Expectation-resource (Suggestive):**

The name can only be partially justified by the term "suggestive", since according to this function the type expects information of a certain sort and is ready to accept it as an important resource for himself. But “suggestion” as a suggestion in its manipulative meaning distorts the name of the function.

Its constructive use is still presumably associated with the expectation and consumption of resources. Therefore, I am inclined to call this function the "expectation-resource", and to correlate suggestion with the entire SUPERID block.

Expectation, just like other functions, has its positive and negative side. The positive side is that a type is forced to somehow expect resource support from society or its individual representatives. The negative side of this function is manifested when this function expects another person to implement programs to benefit it but are not beneficial to the other person.

**2/1 Conservative-critical (PoLR):**

Rapid exhaustion, easy excitability, hysterical readiness, infantilism, weakened control or even its complete absence.

To adapt, in the structure of the psyche, there must be a place for non-standard reactions that reacts sharply to external influences, so as not to miss a moment that is dangerous for survival.  Such a place could play the role of a guard post.

Parasitic complexes can form from the spontaneous development of some internal processes.

Creative vs. PoLR:

If an extremely developed and conscious function can be contrasted with an extremely infantile, trusting, uncritically accepting function, then it would be natural to contrast a creative, innovative, searching, bold, risk-taking function with a dogmatic, conservative, cautious function.

The creative and dogmatic positions can be considered as polar, and this polarity can be described in psychoanalytic terms so that creativity will be compared with the development and awareness of relations with the environment, and dogmatism - with a cautious position of an infantile nature.

**2/2 Motivational-mobilization (Mobilizing):**  

Key in the formation of physiological tone and the transfer of the carrier to a working state, naturally understood as mobilization, which is preceded by a certain resource motivation (within the Suggestive). This function is an indicator of the degree of satisfaction of needs, and, from early childhood, retains its infantile character. It is distinguished by timidity and is in dire need of support from the outside, and therefore is maximally susceptible to manipulation.

Examples:

When ILE get positive Si resource reinforcement he responds with an involuntary Fe positively colored release.  In the case of non-receipt of the expected Si resource, the ILE’s emotional reaction will be negative, and the expected immersion in Ni concentration on the (Ne) work process will not occur.

The EII admires Si beauty, and the EIE is emotionally excited by a demonstration of Se strength.

Note:

This part of the semantics of the Mobilizing is fully reflected by the name "activation" adopted in the Kyiv school (Model G), but the name "mobilizational" more sharply expresses its specialization to transfer a person to an imperative concentration on the work process. The difference between the concepts of "activation" and "mobilization" can be understood as the difference between a simple increase in energy and a directed change in the energy level.

**3/1 Program-potential (Base):** 

The characteristic features of a person's personality appear. This is the level of world perception, world outlook, worldview.

**3/2 Imperative-temporal (Ignoring):** 

Example:

EII imperatively spends his time on that which absorbs the negative emotional (-Fe) flow coming from other people, and for EIE the main object of concentration is establishing relationships (+Fi).

**4/1 Communicative-probing (Creative):** 

The “Creative” function tries to show its capabilities in the best light, which mobilizes its creative activity. However, this name reflects its outer manifestation. At a deeper level, it establishes a communication channel with the environment and the degree of adequacy to the environment is checked. Here the psyche establishes contact with the environment. The environment is probed to obtain operational information about its state, which corresponds to the orienting reflex. 

**4/2 Implementation-technological (Demonstrative):** 

Of course, it can be used as demonstrative, but this is a secondary possibility. For example, Te Demonstrative is distinguished by high efficiency, and, at the vital level, an ILE considers it his duty to perform physical work well when there is a need for it, first as a kind of service.

Demonstrativeness here corresponds to the quality of the finished product and is not something manipulative. Is the ideal product just demonstrativeness? Demonstrativeness as a kind of bragging or show-off does not correspond to the meaning of this function. This is an honest and difficult result that can only be achieved through hard work. Without such work, applications and advances that go through the Creative function will remain at the level of conversations.

The main product of EIE is the formation of new potential opportunities.

The Demonstrative is motivated by other people.  If such motivation does not occur, then a person does not know what to do.

**Achieving goals: ILE**

1) Static Ring:

Ne and Se determine goals because they set the image of generalized values.

Ti and Fi rationally process and adjust goals.

2) Vital Ring:

Te sets the technological and Fe the energy support means of achieving goals. 

Ni and Si determine the time and consumer parameters of the process of achieving the goal.

The position of the 8 elements in Model A are divided into seven subsets.

3 identified by Ausra:

1. Active-Passive (mental or vital)
2. Inert-Contact, (degree of interaction with the environment.)
3. Producing-Accepting, (issuing or receiving.)

4 more subsets:

4. Program-Potential (strong or weak).
5. Evaluative-Situational (4D/1D vs 3D/2D)
6. Verbal-Laboratory (valued or unvalued)
7. Bold-Cautious

**1. Active-Passive (Mental-Vital):**

The concepts of "active-passive" in relation to functional rings is relative. 

Ausra called mental functions active because here, she believed, the mode of action is formed, and the first step is taken towards the goal. In addition, the formed mode of action is largely conscious-or, if necessary, can be relatively easily realized. The functions of the vital ring are classified as passive. This is because they only work out programs formed on the corresponding functions of the mental ring and represent sequences of bodily impulses leading to a purposeful physical action.

Thus, programs are implemented through concentration in the Imperative-Temporal (Ignoring). Similarly, probing (Creative) verbal descriptions of the final production turn into the final product itself in the Implementation-Technological (Demonstrative).

Ausra says: "As for the thinking activity of the mental ring it is productive and follows the automatic activity of the vital ring of the dual." Ausra believes that what is happening in the external world simultaneously gives birth to a thought in the mental ring and motor reactions in the vital. And then she adds: “The motor activity of the vital ring is just as automatic as the thinking activity of the mental”. That is, in this statement both rings are, in a sense, recognized as active, but this activity is automatic. Such activity must be understood simply as excitability, as the presence of some kind of work in these rings, and not at all as a manifestation of initiative.

Therefore, it seems there is no semantic grounds for attributing predominant activity or passivity to any of these rings.  But let us assign to them the concepts of mental and vital, which most adequately express the semantics of these rings.

--------------------

The idea that the structure of a mental function may include material objects significantly expands its semantics, since from a purely internal activity it receives a relation not simply to external manifestations, but also to the independent existence of the products of these external manifestations.  

In the case of materialized products - specific things: a cooked dinner, a sewn dress, a built house, or an assembled car – looks like a miracle that they are a product of mental activity. Here, the function as its own product continues to retain its immanent meaning even in the form of a completely separate and distinct thing. But this meaning was included in the definition of the function, when we said that the function is both the process of the work of an element of the structure of the psyche and its product.

But if for an (intuitive) ideal product such an understanding of the function is perceived as natural, then, in the case of a materialized product, a protest may arise against attributing specific things to the sphere of mental function. And in vain!.

-------------------

It is assumed that between the Mental and Vital rings there is a continuous exchange of information flows. So not only the Vital ring receives control impulses from the Mental, but the Mental also receives from the Vital signals that help to continuously correct the internal model of the environment. If we use such a contrast as acceptance-productivity, then, as Ausra writes, "the Mental ring can be called acceptance, but this is correct only in relation to the perceived information, on the basis of which the Vital ring of the dual acts."

From this point of view, both the Mental and Vital rings can be assessed, sometimes as acceptance, sometimes as productive.

----------------------

Ausra stated:

"Everyone is quick to give advice, correction, amendments, control from their Mental ring. This is its function. The function of the Vital ring is to act on its own."

But, of course, vital activity can lead by "do as I do".

---------------------

**2. Inert-Contact:**  

Inert functions accumulate information-energy potential and set programs and values, which is very difficult to adjust and change.

Contact functions shapes and uses these programs.  They contact products and tools that are relatively easy to change and adjust and are depending on the changing situation.

It is easy to understand why Ausra called functions directly related to the external environment contact. It is more difficult to explain why functions not directly related to the external environment can be called inert.

One explanation is that inert functions gradually accumulate information and resist changes in what is in them. As Ausra says, "Inert blocks form a protective ring, through which information is accumulated."

**Inert sensorics (Accumulating material values, including space):**

Strong/inert sensorics is easy to understand as an attitude towards accumulation of wealth. But how can we understand weak/inert sensorics?  This can be understood in LIE and EIE, who know how to create comfort, but it does not seem that such a feature is inherent in LII and EII.

For LII and EII a material values fixation will have a shade of negativism due to the increased inclination of these types to asceticism and the emergence of such aphorisms as "not by bread alone".

LIE and EIE have a different modality of fixation on material values, since they have Se Mobilizing that ​​encourages active “get going” activity.

**Inert intuition (accumulating ideal values):**

It seems plausible that types with strong/inert intuition (ILE, IEI, ILI, IEE) have a common desire to accumulate ideal values. But it seems unlikely that LSE or ESE should prefer ideal values ​​to material ones.

What could the accumulation of time (Ni) mean? Does it refer to free time?  Or perhaps these are creative processes that lead to the creation of conditions that facilitate the release of time.

LSI and ESI will be negatively fixated on ideal values, whereas LSE and ESE will be ‘wound up’ by them.  (Translator’s note: Does ‘wound up’ mean “mobilized”?  And is this sentence only referring to Ne?)

**Contact instrumental properties:**

On the contrary, the position of Ne/Ni in contact blocks will mean an emphasis on instrumentality, but here the modality will depend on the function.

Example of Instrumental modalities for ILE:

Ti: Creative. Se: Extreme. Si: Readiness to accept and use the expectational theme. Te: Productive materialization.

**Ausra’s explanations of Tactical-Strategic:**

The inert ring has the general modality of value, and the contact ring has the modality of an instrument. The latter, for example, could mean that those who have Se/Si in their contact blocks are able to give money to their partners relatively easily: as a loan, as a credit, as a gift, transfer as a charity, become sponsors, etc. On this basis Ausra believed that such people easily take on the role of patrons, and therefore they can be called that. “A patron is a patron because he does not delve into other people’s problems and does not give far-reaching advice, but only patronizes and helps. Things and money are not an end in themselves for them, but only a means of contact” However, she also suggested other names: “Patron”, “Philanthropist”, and even “Tactician”. The latter, on the basis that “they are capable of giving tactical advice and short-term financial assistance.” As for short-term financial assistance, this fully justifies the names philanthropists and patrons, but giving superficial tactical advice is probably possible even without being a tactician. In the same text there is also the following reasoning: “Tacticians have Ne/Ni in the inert blocks. Therefore, their strategic plans are large-scale, and in their strategic goals and means they are inert. Their strategy manifests itself as the general line of behavior of an individual, from which they do not deviate under any circumstances.”

If this is not the definition of a strategist, then what should be the characteristic of a person to consider him a strategist?

Ausra proceeds from the definition that a tactician is someone who gives tactical advice. One could agree with such a definition if such advice is given for tactical reasons. A truer definition of a tactician seems to be one who effectively solves situational problems. A strategist is one who sets global, large-scale, and long-term problems, and strategy is global, large-scale, and long-term planning of one's own or group activities with the setting of fundamental goals. In military affairs, the concept of strategy is associated with setting the main goals, with the direction of the main attack, and tactics deals with solving specific problems leading to the solution of the main problem.

Probably, everyone must solve tactical problems in life. Another thing is how effective such solutions are and how easily a person takes on such problems. If we consider both parameters, we will have to redefine the concept of a socionic “Tactician” as someone who not only effectively solves situational problems, but also easily shows initiative in taking on such problems.

It seems plausible that strategic abilities are determined by the position of Ne in the "A" model, because it is associated with some significant potential opportunity. On the other hand, tactical abilities depend on Se, since will is necessary. The position of Se in the model provides variations in the ability to solve tactical problems.

**Ausra’s explanations of Contact-Inert:**

It is quite adequate to compare the inert ring with a core that accumulates values, and the contact ring with a protective shell that takes on the pressure of the environment. The core is responsible for the stability of human individuality, and the shell ensures adaptation to changing environmental parameters. Ausra says that "contact functions form a protective ring of the dyad, which protects from unexpected stresses and frustrations." Apparently, we are talking about a dual pair. In this case, all eight IMEs are in the contact rings of the duals, which allows for a comprehensive perception and evaluation of the impact of the environment.

The means used by the contact ring are everything with which one can contact the environment. This can include narration, command, questions, answers, advice, discussions, bickering, forceful pressure, emotionalization, services, joint actions such as dancing, fighting, or digging a ditch, gifts, robbery, theft. In general, everything is used here with the help of which one person can convey a significant signal to another.

What is in the inert blocks are allowed only with sufficient trust, while what is on the contact functions is put into use at every convenient opportunity. The tendency of contact functions can be denoted by the expression "everything is for sale".

**3. Accepting–Producing:**

Acceptance functions: Defines the goals and assessments.  Accumulates, targets, and assess information.

Producing functions: Defines the generalized form of the product and the characteristics of the attitude towards the product and between producers in the productive process.  Works with technological and production programs.

The producing shell protects the accepting core.

Ausra writes that acceptance blocks perceive an incoming signal either "as a challenge that requires mobilization for resistance and defending one's point of view or one's interests, or as an order that requires the same mobilization for the sake of adaptation." According to acceptance blocks, the result of interaction depends on the balance of power between the partners, and any means that are used in this case are understood by each of the partners as acceptable.

Productive blocks do not imply a struggle - nothing is won through them, but recognition is expected. If your proposals are rejected, that is, according to Berne, you get a “prick”, and if from people with whom you do not expect any competition on this issue, then this is perceived as injustice.

Within the framework of the “core-shell” metaphor, the core is played by the acceptance ring, because it can carry relatively greater loads, compared to the productive one. The acceptance ring may or may not accept the signal coming to it, depending on the characteristics of this signal.

The functions of the productive ring expect positive support, praise. If a blow is dealt to the productive ring, it is perceived extremely painfully. If you remember any case when you were humiliated, then this will be one of the possible examples on this topic. The acceptance ring collects and gives out information, but this information is not subject to discussion. When trying to discuss information of this kind, a person experiences a feeling of awkwardness, as if he were letting something slip or revealing some secret. On the other hand, the topics of the productive block aspects easily become the subject of discussion, but this can only be done with the “appropriate” types, otherwise what you say will be perceived as something incomplete, empty, or inappropriate.

**4. Program-Potential (Strong-Weak / 4D & 3D – 2D & 1D):**

**Example: ILE**

Potential:

SeFi / SiFe: Impact of the external environment and subjective reaction. 

(Involved: Sensorics and Ethics.  Both are perceived as absolute as they are recognized as really existing and not subject to detached intuitive and logical correction. Imperative standards.).

Program:

NeTi / NiTe: Sets the objective parameters of activity.

(Detached: Intuition and Logic)

**5. Verbal-Laboratory (Valued-Unvalued):**

Verbal: Sets the topics that are acceptable for discussion, what can and should be talked about and discussed in the process of developing a group opinion.

Laboratory: Sets the forms of practical activity, what should be done with full concentration, without wasting mobilized energy on extraneous conversations. All aspects included in the first group have the general meaning of "conversational".

--------------------

Example: ILE

Conversational:

Ne: What is being talked about. Ti: The process. Si: Aesthetic component. Fe: Emotional component.

Laboratory:

Se:  Volitional component of the work being done. Fi:  The relationships that arise in the process of work. Ni:  The duration and the concentration with which the work must be performed. Te:  The technological process itself, underlying the work being performed.

-----------------

Conversational aspect topics in verbal blocks is a kind of debugging of the algorithms of possible activity, so that the activity itself is free from errors. Verbal modeling of possible errors, absurdities and misunderstandings is done here using various forms of irony, which looks sharp, interesting, funny and prevents the repetition of the ridiculed situation in practice. Such a discussion is of a detailed nature. That is, everything is discussed, right down to individual actions. "Arguments, discussions, attacks, claims. All this is at the level of an intellectual game or helping those who do not understand".

The EGO block topic is not afraid of a humorous and ironic tone, because a person is confident in his competence and thinks about it actively, consciously, and independently. At the same time, a person easily accepts responsibility for this topic, and his conscience is calm, because this topic does not affect him. On the other hand, the SUPERID topic is largely closed for a person, and he eagerly catches any information on the SUPERID aspects, subconsciously hoping that this will help him solve his problems, and therefore he does not care in what form this information comes. Even if he is scolded and read on this topic, he will perceive it as a form of useful information and as a kind of care for him.

Ausra writes:

"In a group of people who’s verbal and laboratory blocks coincide, there is not a shadow of suspicion that someone does not trust someone, thinks differently than they say, is angry, offended, etc. But there is so much fun, jokes, and ease in them." 

For Alpha Quadra, his is because they rely on the same meaning (Ne), use a speech style that is perceived by all participants in the same way (Ti), get the same aesthetic pleasure (Si) - hence, a lot of humor, jokes, "gags", their emotions (Fe) have a similar coloring.

Blocks form a collectivity when the members of the group at the subconscious level feel cohesion, easily manifested in joint actions. Here, conversations are no longer appropriate - they could only destroy the charm of unity. Of course, this does not mean that people, working together, do not say a word - it means that the verbal component of communication is extremely limited here, and is largely determined by such a parameter as caution. "Only objective information is transmitted, what was seen or heard, without personal comments.

They act without discussing, only exchanging opinions in the course of the work".

The collectivity induced by the laboratory ring becomes the reason that situations do not arise in which one of their own could be accused of something. This is because everything is done together, in a single "laboratory field", where "there are no right and wrong". But if someone starts talking on a topic that is "non-verbal" for specific people, this immediately causes caution, suspicion, and rejection. Such a reaction manifests itself in physical tension and is not always conscious.

**6. Evaluative-Situational:**

Evaluative (4D and 1D) aspects define invariant, unconditional, absolute values, what they strive for, what they are proud of.

Situational (3D and 2D) aspects define virtual, exchangeable, relative, situational values. Evaluative-situational blockings provide a distinction between careless and prudent.

**For ILE:**

**Invariant evaluated values:**

Mental:

1) Potential capabilities (Ne)

2) Relationship (Fi) that can be established with him.

Vital:

3) Well-being and health (Si)

4) Performance, or productivity (Te).

**Situational, instrumental values:**

Mental:

1) Speech & Social Status (Ti)

2) Parameters of will (Se)

Vital:

3) Emotionalization (Fe)

4) Identification with the flow of time, concentration (Ni)

-------

Ausra: “Mental evaluative functions understand better and therefore evaluate others, and vital ones are tuned to receive evaluation from others.”

This means evaluative mental functions first evaluate others, and only secondarily expect evaluation of themselves. Conversely, the vital evaluative functions expect evaluation of themselves, and only secondarily evaluate others.

A personality is far from indifferent to how others evaluate their Mental evaluative functions. By projecting its evaluative function onto others, the personality, one way or another, also assumes the possibility of evaluation by others.

Similar reasoning is applicable to the vital part of the evaluative ring.  For example, Demonstrative needs a positive evaluation of its products and is tuned to such an evaluation, since this is an indicator of the individual's successful adaptation to the environment. Therefore, since the Demonstrative belongs to the Vital Ring, it apparently remains sensitive to external evaluation, but it can act as a sensitive organ capable of evaluating a similar element of another psyche.

The personality is configured to thoroughly perceive and understand the topics of the evaluation functions as fundamental.

------

Example: ILE

Of primary importance and essential to personal development and not indifferent to assessment by others:

1. Ne: Mental, intellectual, and physical abilities and potential of other people.
2. Fi:  Relationships that are maintained between people.
3. Si:  Health and well-being relative to a specific moment in time and place.
4. Te: Technological side of work.  Productivity.

Of secondary importance and manifested in the background in various qualities as a mere means for self-realization:

1. Ti:  Career and official position in society.
2. Se: The ability to exert force on others.  
3. Fe: The ability to manipulate one's emotional states and reactions.
4. Ni:  Spending free time on a variety of forms and rest.

--------------

This may mean, for example, that when an ILE must choose between a career (Ti) and relationships (Fi) with people close to him, he will most likely neglect a career in favor of relationships.  This, of course, does not mean that such people are completely indifferent to a career, but its value strongly depends on the situation.

---------------

According to Ausra:

1) Evaluative functions perceive gratitude as inappropriate, but highly value recognition.  Conversely, situational functions need gratitude and encouragement.

2) Evaluative functions represent a general lifestyle, a “worldview, world understanding and world perception”.   In contact, the situational functions are associated with superficial social activity.  They can be compared with public morality, which often contains a large share of hypocrisy.  

3)  Evaluative functions represents continuity. In contrast, the situational ring is compared with discontinuity, or discreteness.  Continuously here means always, constantly, without interruption, and discretely means only sometimes, only when necessary, only as a response to environmental pressure.

----------------

The duals' worldview is based on identical archetypes, and under suitable conditions it should not be difficult for duals to develop a single attitude to life. However, the same set of IMEs is present in the evaluative ring of a quasi-identical and Conflicting pairs, but the arrangement of these aspects is different.

-----------------

Four types of evaluative-situational rings with differing worldviews and social morality:

1) NeFiSiTe – TiSeFeNi 2) FeNiTiSe – SiTeNeFi 3) FeSiNeTi – NiTeSeFi 4) SeFiNiTe - NeTiFeSi

(One of the 35 archetypes of correct socionic fours)

These fours use two dichotomies. The basis for such dichotomies can be chosen in three semantically dependent different ways.

**7. Bold-Cautious (Objective–Relational for extroverts / Relational-Objective for introverts):**

Within the framework of the "core-shell" metaphor, the core here is the Bold ring, and the shell is the Cautious one.

The cautious shell protects the bold core. These concepts suggests that the bold side of personality is a fundamental value, and the cautious one is more mobile and easier to change.

-------------------------------------------

ILE:

Role: Mental, contact, accepting, situational, laboratory, criterial, potential, reproductive

Suggestive: Passive, contact, accepting, evaluative, verbal, criterial, potential

PoLR: Mental, inert, productive, evaluative, laboratory, impulsive, potential

Mobilizing: Passive, inert, productive, situational, verbal, impulsive, potential

Base: Mental, inert, accepting, evaluative, verbal, criterial, program, volitional, leading, expansive, inductive

Ignoring: Passive, inert, acceptance, situational, laboratory, criterion, program

Creative: Mental, contact, productive, situational, verbal, impulsive, program

Demonstrative: Passive, contact, productive, evaluative, laboratory, impulsive, program

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  

**EGO:**

**Program-potential (Base):** Mental, inert, accepting, evaluative, verbal, program, objective, active, volitional, leading, expansive, inductive, reproductive.

Base actively reacts to everything related to its IME. This accepting function accumulates highly structured information and contains and stores programs, worldview schemes and models of the environment.

This Base function can “get stuck”, avoids changing the subject (inertia) and strives to continuously reproduce and enrich its content (reproductivity).

When in a difficult situation, the Base function does not get lost, but becomes active, feeling competent, strong, and confident. It easily and naturally accepts the challenge of the environment. It welcomes complicated situations, because it gives the Base function an opportunity to demonstrate its best abilities and make a greater contribution to the process of self-realization. The Base function easily perceives the structure and any features of such a situation and quickly adapts to it. If manipulation is necessary to obtain the maximum effect, for example, it is necessary to lie – the Base lies with a clear conscience.

Ausra says: "Can this be called fantasizing or diplomatic tactical games or tricks? For the bearer of the type, such behavior is only a form of everyday art that decorates life. People are told not what the case actually is, but what the bearer of the type considers most appropriate at the moment, what they deserve from his point of view. But carriers of the type behave this way only with those whom they do not respect and do not love, whom they do not care about."

This function expresses the primary attitude of the personality, and putting it into practice, a person is categorical, demanding, intrusive, therefore it can be also designated as strong-willed. The individual tries to subordinate everyone around him to his concepts, which are a projection of expansiveness.

According to this function, a person speaks, advises, actively participates in a conversation, argues, creatively develops, and processes the information coming to him. Here are the values ​​that set the meaning of life and are the basis on which the ultimate goals for the self-realization of the individual are formed. According to the Base, a person selects the signals he needs, carrying information from the outside world. Moreover, The Base easily creates new ideas, images, and concepts. It contributes to the adaptation of society to objective reality. Here, new norms, new standards are born and created, aimed at an increasingly rational adaptation of society to the environment. It is possible to convince the Base function only with compelling evidence and specific examples. But it is impossible to simply confuse, force it to abandon its opinion, because here a person not only has a deep understanding, but sees the corresponding problems in a comprehensive, multifaceted, and systemic manner.

The Base can reproduce global standards and perceives objects in all the diversity of its manifestations. In a broad sense, the Base thoroughly understands an object via observation, evaluation, and study.  This includes not only physical objects and phenomena, but also informational entities, which can include relationships between people. This function expresses a person’s will, the will that confronts the will of other people.

If this function is damaged, then the person loses the meaning of life. “To break a person” means to suppress, “crush,” discredit, destroy this function. Anomalies that arise in the process of development of this function manifest themselves as psychological disorders of varying severity.

Ausra says that in no case should a person be “praised according to this function, one can provoke and slightly support”. That is, support according to this function should not be intrusive. Here, praise is perceived as something inappropriate, artificial, like outright flattery, after all, according to this function, a person knows his own worth, and, most importantly, keeps under intellectual control any topic available to him that corresponds to it.

**Communicative-probing (Creative):** Mental, contact, productive, situational, verbal, programmatic, relational, creative, manipulative, informative, orientational and even advertising.

This function is productive and makes contact, that is, searches the environment for what is possible for a given personality and a given function product, is responsible for interaction with the environment, probing and checking the result of the previous step of the personality’s adaptation to the environment by its reactions. The output of this function is of an informative nature.

According to this function, the personality tries to do everything, so its information product is favorably received by the environment. Here the individual imperatively strives to earn praise, which confirms the high quality of its created product and recognizes the value it creates in the immediate environment. Therefore, it uses its creative abilities for the best, winning presentation of its product, but this creativity is of an “advertising-packaging” nature, since the essential creative process of the primary creation of the product, its invention, occurs on the Base. According to this function, the individual is capable of consciously manipulating the environment and its agents.

The Creative function offers the environment its mental product, as a kind of trial balloon, launched into the environment with the almost unconscious goal of obtaining feedback. Hoping for a positive reaction from the environment, the function tries to design its product as acceptable as possible for the environment, activating its creative potential. According to this function, the individual takes positive initiative.

One of the names for this function Ausra proposed is the “orientation” function, however, the concepts of communication and probing fully cover the concept of orientation.  It would be incorrect to emphasize the manipulative capabilities of the function in its name, since manipulation is a form of negative intervention in the environment and should be mentioned here only as a negative possibility, which, however, very easily becomes dominant in a vicious social environment. Also, it would be redundant to introduce the term “productive” into the name of this function since productivity is a common parameter of the four functions in the “A” model. The same can be said about the concept of “contact function”.

According to it, a person communicates, proves, convinces, jokes, creates, provides services, makes gifts, recognizes the right of another to equality, gives "strokes", up to the point that according to it, something is imposed on others. And according to it, the individual is inclined to criticize others for unreasonable, inappropriate, thoughtless waste of energy, since, in connection with his typological features, he understands the scope of this function better than carriers of other types.

Ausra writes about this function: “Many reactions with the Creative function are just reactions by which people around you are, as it were, tested, probed. This is the reason for many jokes, which, if they are out of place, are quickly abandoned."

According to this function, people brag about themselves, and therefore for successful contact with them, it is enough to gently support them, and when appropriate, express your admiration with compliments. Such admiration, if it is not manipulative, is precisely one of the possible forms of feedback. This same feature of the function, in the case of reverse manipulation, allows you to get a person to be able to tell more than he intended.

Regarding this function Ausra writes: “On the EGO, according to the Creative element, there is a comparison of the potential possibilities of individual objects and subjects, as a result of which a logical feeling of knowledge of how these objects relate to each other appears.”

This remark applies not only to logical types. This function itself has a primary-generalized logical character in all types, since it is oriented toward verbal production, and the aspect Ti is at the basis of its semantics. And if a person develops confidence according to this function, then this confidence can easily be transformed into knowledge.  To do this, it is enough to collect the necessary number of arguments. This transformation occurs especially quickly in a group of like-minded people who support the bearer of such knowledge, provide him with favorable criticism, and make useful additions. It is important that a person prepares information on this function not so much for himself as an intermediate summary, but for others, whose recognition is the most important element of self-realization for him. He tries to share such information even when no one asks him about it.

Such information, being valuable, is a good means of interesting and attracting people who can become a support in the further development of the ideas found. This function continuously and unconsciously probes the environment with the aim of discovering in it signals important to the individual, allowing him to correct his own behavior, accept or reject challenges and consciously or unconsciously influence the internal model of the environment.

If this function is damaged, a person loses the ability to be creative, becomes inadequate in communication and loses interest in it, which often manifests itself as cynicism, alienation, autism.

**General description of Ego:**

Maximum activity block. Main block. The meaning of life. Optimal self-realization zone.  It assesses valuable information.

EGO is an energy-informational zone of the personality associated with maximum positive self-identification, i.e. identification of one's own volitional acts with the results of their corresponding individual actions and systemic activity. A mature EGO is characterized by the personality's ability to take responsibility for one's own behavior. This zone is much more accessible to consciousness than any other. This zone also has access to a higher level of consciousness compared to other functions - reflection and self-reflection. Reflection is the ability to think over one's actions with varying degrees of detail. Self-reflection is the ability to see and objectively evaluate oneself from the outside.

In the development and maturation of the EGO, there comes a special moment when a person achieves a high degree of confidence in his behavior. This confidence has nothing to do with self-confidence or arrogance a person may have. This confidence is based on its subject of interest being revealed before the inner gaze of the individual. He sees the subject in full, with all its internal and external connections, he quickly and easily delves into any problems associated with this subject, is ready to answer any questions concerning it. This determines the maturity of the EGO, which does not always correspond to age. Most of the time, a mature person thinks about the subject of his interest, and with careful observation this can become a good basis for diagnosing his type.

A person can achieve internal fusion, identification with an object very naturally. When a person reaches this level, then, as Ausra writes, "he knows better what the world expects from him, what the world hopes for. This is the idea of ​​​​oneself through the prism of the world."

EGO is the area of ​​​​conscious influence on the world, although very often people do not realize this. In this block, maximum self-identification, and identification with objects of the external world that correspond to the archetype of the block is carried out. This is the block of adequate self-esteem. Various types of defeat of this block are expressed, among other things, in a distortion of self-esteem. This is a block of deep study of a certain parameter of the external world. The implementation of which a person demands recognition adequate to his abilities. Zone in which a person can act completely independently. The area of ​​creative realization of the personality. It is here that a person can be most useful to society.

A special state is associated with the EGO, which can be called the experience of self, when a person feels that he keeps all his abilities under control, forms his own idea of ​​the world, puts forward goals adequate to his position in the world, confidently makes decisions and achieves their implementation.

The EGO, within its capabilities, implements exactly what is necessary for society.  But the personality does not always realize this, but it clearly feels the imperative pressure coming from within, as a passionate desire to do exactly this business as its calling. A realized EGO provides a sense of productivity, validity, and prospects for one's business, since it is needed by other people, is fairly valued by society, and brings a person deep satisfaction, and all this together is experienced as freedom.

When this block is damaged, a person loses the ability to be creative and switches to a parasitic or semi-parasitic lifestyle.

Ausra writes: “The EGO block is a kinetic block, and when it is realized, the individual is brave and fearless. He always knows, is sure that he will find a way out, and even likes difficult situations. A lot is achieved through this block, because it is here that the conscious will of the individual is realized.”

Suppression of the EGO, the inferiority of its work is not only the absence of self-realization, but also the loss of life prospects, deep dissatisfaction with oneself, a constant feeling of guilt, a complex of “unfulfilled”, “failed”. If this condition becomes severe and chronic, the person begins to go downhill and can easily become an alcoholic or drug addict.

If a person makes a mistake on the EGO block, he provides all the necessary arguments to justify himself, shows how it could have happened, finds options in which he could have been right, and in any case waits for full proof of his mistake. Having received such proof, he feels gratitude, experiences the incident as an important life experience associated with the acquisition of new knowledge, and does not repeat the mistake itself.

**SUPER-EGO**

**Adaptive-load (Role):** Mental, contact, acceptance, situational, laboratory, potential, objective, reproductive, normative, role, protective.

This function is accepting, contact and reproductive, i.e. information is collected and accumulated through it because of contact with the environment, and the entire content of the function is continuously self-reproducing. The nature of the information accumulated here strongly depends on the adjacent Conservative-Critical (PoLR) function in the block. However, this also applies to all other blocks. The Adaptive-Load (Role) is configured to perceive the stress aspect of the environment, extreme conditions, and force pressure.

Extreme conditions are not only such grandiose events as natural disasters, but the need also to live in harsh climatic conditions, war, or long expeditions. At the socionic level of generalization, these are also smaller-scale circumstances that may seem insignificant from the outside, but they differ in that when they occur, the personality is distracted from the main object of its interest and is forced to fully engage in protecting its mental and physical integrity. And then it has no time for the "higher matters" that the EGO should be engaged in. These are situations in which it is difficult or impossible to realize one's EGO. These may include social circumstances of a person's life, often forcing him to live at the level of survival. Environmental pressures on this function is the most important factor of individual and evolutionary-species adaptation.

This function evaluates the environment from the point of view of threat, danger, pressure, aggression and develops, mobilizes means of resisting the negative impact of the environment.

This function can be called the adaptive-load function (Role). This is the meaning and the information.  According to the aspect of this function, it is undesirable to put pressure on a person since this can act as a provocation and lead to an inadequate reaction. The response may be unexpectedly harsh.

The assessment of this function as a normative one, which some authors encounter, may be partly justified by its semantics, in the sense that in non-stressful situations, in its manifestations, it gravitates toward considering the norms accepted in the environment of the individual's existence. The very need to consider norms and moral requirements can be considered and perceived as a kind of external pressure, and sometimes as an extreme load. Of course, here the nature of the norms is directly related to the IME. However, when a load appears, the personality quickly gains such a potential for this function that, at a minimum, it equalizes or significantly exceeds the applied external effort. Therefore, it must be recognized that the name of this function as a normative one reflects a particular case of its functioning.

This function is also called a role function. However, such a name greatly reduces the adaptive meaning of this function, especially since the personality, depending on the situation, can organize the role design of its activity for any function. An additional argument against this name is that the concept of a role has a social, not a psychophysiological meaning.

In a pathological variant of the development of this function, a person can become highly irritable and deflated or lose the ability to resist the environment.

**Conservative-critical (PoLR):** Mental, inert, productive, evaluative, laboratory, potential, relative, place of least resistance, painful, problematic.

This function is productive and inert, that is, the information content of this function tends to resist changes. At the same time, it is productive, since it forms a reaction to stressful, traumatic information coming through the Role. It is this that determines the object of the relationship and gets stuck on it. The main generalized moral problem of each person is formed on this function. This is a vulnerable spot in the mental structure of the personality. A person reacts very sharply to any signal on the aspect of this function, is often touchy, vulnerable, and sensitive to any criticism. Ausra, using Kempinsky's term, called this function the place of least resistance. And this is correct, in that according to this function, a person is easy to offend, embarrass, insult. But at the same time, a person according to this function does not tolerate interference and impudence and, according to its theme, easily goes on the counterattack, makes a scandal, sharply criticizes the aggressor and, defending himself, is ready to develop the maximum resistance of which he is only capable. Negative experience accumulates according to this function, which later becomes the basis for better adaptation to the environment in its objective or subjective aspect. But the subject according to this function is also critical of himself. He avoids demonstrating his capabilities, shows a tendency to hide, to leave in the shadow his position and what relates to its information content, be it work, talent, will or something else. And this is because a person always feels dissatisfaction with himself, is always dissatisfied with the results of work by this IME, considers it unacceptable and immodest to show them to others, never brags on the corresponding topic. On the topic of this function, a person constantly experiences a vague unconscious anxiety, which makes him try to do some business, but it is difficult for him to realize and formulate the corresponding goal, because of which such attempts easily fade away at the very beginning. Everything that goes on the aspect of this function requires an increased expenditure of energy from a person, and many things are endlessly delayed and, as a rule, are not brought to completion. According to this function, remorse easily arises if a person even simply feels that he is preventing someone from demonstrating his abilities according to the IME, and according to this same function, a person is afraid of becoming the object of even completely harmless jokes, not to mention irony and open mockery. But at the same time, he suffers and is tormented if no one is interested in this side of his life. A person is in dire need of support and cover for this function, it is difficult for him to discuss everything that concerns this function, and his own opinion on the corresponding topic is very unstable and easily changes depending on the circumstances. If there is uncertainty on the topic of the function, this is experienced hard, and all attempts are made to eliminate such uncertainty. Here, a lot, if not everything, depends on what others demonstrate to a person. The range of experiences for this function is very wide: from embarrassment, readiness to modestly hide behind the backs of others to furious indignation and resentment. Communication on the topic of this function is extremely difficult. If a person does not receive adequate support for this function, then, this can lead to deep disappointment in people and life. But if the cover of the function is provided, the individual can not only calmly look at his abilities associated with this function, but also teach someone who finds himself in an even weaker position.

"An individual according to this function collects any information about everything that "feeds" the corresponding feeling". For some, this is a sense of time, for others, the desire to maintain good relations with people, and for some, an aversion to any manifestations of aggression.

This function, being inert, is distinguished by a high degree of conservatism, but being productive and protecting the ideas of the personality corresponding to the information content of this function, it manifests itself in a critical attitude to any encroachment on the attitudes existing here. This is the primary taboo. Conservative values ​​​​are stored here. According to this function, a person tries to be correct, does not show sympathy, experiences deep doubts, worries whether he treats the object correctly and honestly, is afraid of a breakdown and is simply nervous if he is forced to somehow show himself according to it. Primary ethical imperatives are formed here.  At the level of the ultimate communication, the cardiovascular system corresponds to it.

Here, as in the heart, is the basic, the main thing. The main thing is in the head, which corresponds to the Base function. And the main thing is in the heart, which corresponds to the function PoLR. The loss of this value means the loss of orientation in this world. If this function for some reason is destroyed or deformed, a person becomes restless, only technically performing his work, but deprived of illusions and the charm of the ideal, and life for him loses one of the most important components of its meaning, and he can easily commit suicide.

According to the PoLR, a person is not able to control the situation associated with it, and his behavior in this case can be conditionally called “anti-aspect”. Someone does not know or does not notice where and how time goes, but for him it turns out to be a universal equivalent with which everything is compared, and someone does not take into account what is accepted to wear and can easily turn out to be an original in this regard; someone does not recognize predetermined rules of behavior, but at the same time does not impose their own, and someone does not understand why thinking must necessarily be driven into the narrow framework of logical syllogisms, which makes such thinking extremely boring, while there is an infinite number of ways in which you can, communicating with others, vividly and unexpectedly formulate your thought. If the informational content of this function is the aspect of extroverted ethics, then the individual may seem dispassionate, but when he is provoked, his emotions turn out to be unbridled, like those of an enraged bull. If the informational aspect of this function is extroverted sensorics, then the owner of such a function may seem weak-willed, in the sense that he is not capable of exerting forceful pressure on others, but he does not consider this acceptable.

A situation of “provocative despair” or “quiet hysteria” may arise for this function, which in general can be expressed by the words “oh, you think I am such and such, well, then you will see me as even more incapable than I really am.”

Examples:

"Oh, you think I'm stupid and incapable of learning, so you'll see me even more stupid and incapable of anything."

"Oh, you think I'm ugly, so I'll dress like that, and I'll have such makeup and such a hairstyle that your eyes will pop out of your heads."

"Oh, you think I'm lazy and incapable of working, so I'll do minimum work for you so that you'll get it."

"Oh, you think I'm weak-willed and incapable of resisting pressure, so you'll see it on an even larger scale."

**General description of Super-Ego:**

SUPEREGO makes a person a social being. This psychological imperatively motivates the individual to perform actions that consider group interests. SUPEREGO programs are almost not recognized by the personality, although some of them can be brought to consciousness. Unexpected recognition of such programs can also occur under special circumstances. The imperative pressure of these programs is felt as a certain duty, as an irresistible desire to act in a certain way, to act as if there were some very important values behind it.
