However, an explicit, verbal formulation of this value usually causes difficulties. Moreover, some explicitly formulated values ​​concerning interaction with society may not have a direct relation to what stands behind the SUPEREGO, since these can be uncritically adopted slogans, aphorisms, mottos, sayings, toasts.

The SUPEREGO contains a prohibition program, which is formulated as what cannot be done (PoLR), using such and such means (Role). But at the same time, it is a positive program, which for the carrier of the type looks like a certain obligation and is felt as a duty, the fulfillment of which brings deep satisfaction. The SUPEREGO programs put the personality into a strict framework of prohibitions and duties. Depending on how successfully the personality works out these programs, it develops a sense of its own value. The feeling of its own value is perceived by the personality as an assessment from society and as a sense of its own need. Nevertheless, although this is necessary for the full self-realization of the personality, it is not enough.

The SUPEREGO only sets the form of the ideal to which the personality imperatively strives, but its content is worked out by the EGO programs. SUPEREGO is a subtle mental organ for regulating the well-being of the individual, and this organ requires complete trust from the environment for its effective functioning. Irony, teasing, ridicule according to SUPEREGO are experienced painfully, and praise or a compliment are perceived adequately only if special conditions are met this must be done as if in private, using indirect comparisons.

The best confirmation of the rightness of SUPEREGO is the direct and undemonstrative use of its values, acceptance, or support of the individual by the dual from his ID block. Manipulative imitation is possible here, but it requires a lot of energy and fine tact. The subconscious energy pressure that the individual feels according to SUPEREGO is perceived as an impulse that encourages the implementation of his positive programs. If the quality of the development of these programs does not correspond to some subconscious standard, then the person feels it as frustration of varying intensity, which is subjectively experienced as remorse.

If, according to the SUPEREGO, the individual receives positive feedback from society, then he experiences a sense of self-worth and imperatively tries to do everything that depends on him. Somewhere on the edge of consciousness, a person feels his connection with society, and imperatively strives to ensure that it values ​​him, that he is needed. And the more he is needed, the freer and stronger the person feels and becomes.

The idea of the personality about itself. This is a remarkable discovery of Ausra, since in ego psychology, the most advanced direction in personality psychology, developed based on Freud's ideas, there is still an idea that a person's idea of ​​​​his own personality is formed on the EGO, as the most conscious part of the personality. Although, of course, here we can talk about different projections of the EGO and its different functional implementations.

The better I understand what interests me most in the world, the better I will feel. The more important information I collect for me, the more accurately I will understand the meaning of my life. That is, what others expect from me.

If the implementation of the SUPEREGO block is successful, then the individual feels confident, because he knows what the generalized environment that a person perceives as the world, but which in most cases is realized as the immediate human environment, expects from him. As Ausra says, such a feeling is “the idea of ​​oneself through the prism of the world.”

Although what corresponds to the SUPEREGO theme, a person considers his duty and tries to fulfill it, but the abilities and energy for the full implementation of “good intentions” are not enough here.

One of the manifestations of SUPEREGO is that a person strives to act like a type that is in a socionic SUPEREGO relationship with him. However, the carrier of one type cannot fully reproduce the behavior of the carrier of another type, and therefore it is always only some weakened imitation, which nevertheless has its own completely independent meaning. Thus, ILE’s SUPEREGO is set to "make suffering humanity happy", which in the literal, "energetic" sense, should mean a powerful energetic recharge of each person. However, such recharge, on their scale and with a different intention, is successfully carried out by SEEs, who are with ILEs in the SUPEREGO relationship. ILE has only a subconscious SUPEREGO setting to open a source of such nourishment to people, and his efforts in this direction remain in the realm of “good intentions” and are often utopian, that is, divorced from real life. In such cases, the bearer of the type exceeds the measure of his typical competence, thereby demonstrating the inevitable limitations of a separate unit of the socion, unable to cover the entire range of human possibilities.

On the other hand, SEE, according to his SUPEREGO, subconsciously strives to show people the possibilities of a full existence, but the most he can do is only entertain and inspire them for a limited time. True, he uses this situation for self-affirmation.

SUPEREGO is an instance of social order. Here, the utmost possible objective picture of the environment for the type of carrier is formed, and, in this sense, SUPEREGO is an instrument for reproducing reality, which is what people call the world, and thanks to this, SUPEREGO gives a person the opportunity for primary orientation in what he perceives as objective reality. Here it is appropriate to introduce a distinction between the objective and subjective parts of the environment.

This distinction appears in connection with the different object orientation of logical and ethical types. Although they live in both environments, they relate to them differently. Logicians tend to consider everything as an object, including bearers of subjectivity, while ethicists are ready to attribute subjectivity to “inanimate” nature, since they even feel the real existence of such subjectivity, spiritualize, and personify natural phenomena.

A bearer of the type perceives one part of the environment as an objective reality, as a kind of absolute that cannot be influenced, cannot be changed, and one cannot even have one’s own opinion, but which must be considered and on which one can rely. This is a part of the environment in relation to which the bearer of the type exhibits maximum conformism and extreme caution. From this part of the environment, a person receives a kind of order that must imperatively be fulfilled. This order can be described as “expectation,” a silent expectation on the part of a certain absolute. A person cannot refuse to fulfill this order – otherwise, he feels inferior, experiences dissatisfaction with himself. Ethicists understand and operate in a subjective environment, and receive an order from an objective environment, logicians, on the contrary, understand and operate in an objective environment, and receive an order from a subjective one. This order is perceived as a need to do something important, something that would provide the individual with a high level of self-esteem.

The SUPEREGO is also associated with what can be called the proclaimed, illusory meaning of life, in contrast to the real meaning life, formed on the EGO.

If a person makes a mistake on the SUPEREGO block, he experiences it as a personal tragedy, feels remorse. In this case, he does not even need special evidence - it is enough to point out the obvious consequences of his action. In case of unsuccessful activity, a person develops a conscious or unconscious feeling of guilt, which is formalized by elements of the SUPEREGO and is perceived in terms that the SUPEREGO uses in accordance with its IMEs.

**SUPER-ID**

**Expectation-resource (Suggestive):** Vital, contact, accepting, evaluative, verbal, potential, relative, passive, regulatory, suggestive.

Being vital, this function reflects the features and level of needs. This function can be characterized as passive, which means that according to this function the individual himself does not show activity, but passively waits to receive a signal that is significant for him about the IME. This function is in direct contact with the environment and receives a signal directly from the surrounding world, sensitively reacting to any changes in the material-informational situation, selecting information valuable for the personality and the individual, accumulating the necessary potential, reproducing, and preparing it for further use. The Suggestive, together with the Role, is the first, or input link in the process of the four-stroke metabolic process of transforming information flows perceived by the passive ring of the mental structure of the personality.

This function is sensitive to the information flow, with what can be called a generalized resource. The semantics of this resource is determined by the IME. According to this function, the personality subconsciously expects massive support. It is difficult for a person to create such a resource himself, although he is sensitive to it and desperately needs it. In case of an acute deficit, the carrier of the type himself tries to create this resource, but he does it poorly, primitively, and “home-grown”. The search for the necessary signal according to this function can be expressed as an aimless movement from one place where one can find a suitable source of the resource in another. This is a kind of escape from oneself. However, this is not an active search, when a person knows exactly what he is looking for, but a passive wandering with an unconscious mindset. And at the same time, as soon as the expected signal appears, the person instantly perceives it as what he was looking for. When we say "signal" in this context, then, of course, the subject of the psyche receives a signal. However, the source of this signal can be anything: a person, a thing, an event, an important message. According to this function, a person feels the importance of this IME for his well-being, and comfort, but this feeling is vague and is normally in the background. If the need to satisfy its needs becomes acute, then, as far as possible, a person begins to "fill in the gaps" on his own, but since there are no natural abilities in the IME then high professionalism and perfect execution are far from here. Still, with systematic effort, the required ability can be trained, but it seems that this process develops according to the type of compensation.

Some socionics assess this function as suggestive, but it seems to me that this is the result of a mechanical transfer of the semantics of the corresponding function from the "J" model to the "A" model. The fact is that the "J" model, in comparison with the "A" model, is truncated, and the corresponding function there, as it were, combined the semantics of two functions, and in the "A" model there is an opportunity to divide the functional phenomenology into the suggestive and the Mobilizing. Suggestion in this case, as a manipulative form, is related to the entire SUPERID block.

Motivating factors are determined by:

1) Needs and instincts.

2) The direction of activity, for which the choice of activity is made – motives.

3) Mechanisms of behavior regulation - emotions, desires, aspirations, and attitudes.

If we compare this structure of motivating factors with the entire structure of SUPERID, then it is quite plausible that the Mobilizing correspond to emotions, desires, and aspirations, and Suggestive - needs and attitudes. This function accumulates programs that energetically provide motivation for behavioral acts of the individual.

Suggestive, being accepting, is capable of perceiving even very sharp criticism. When it hears criticism on the topic of the aspect in his direction, he does not perceive it as something offensive, as a manifestation of aggression or an attempt to humiliate him, but, on the contrary, hears in such criticism a hint, a guide to action, and immediately uses the information thus obtained to increase the effectiveness of his life. No matter what a person is reproached for, if it is on the topic of Suggestive, he does not perceive this as a reproach, but will accept it as support. This means that even outwardly negative forms of communication are not rejected, do not become an object of negativity, but are perceived with gratitude. If you criticize a person, for example, for callousness, lack of initiative or frivolity, he immediately realizes that he was wrong and perceives the received message so adequately that you can be sure of his future attitude to the corresponding situations.  This circumstance expands the communicative repertoire of interaction with the individual, when along with positive forms of communication, negative ones can also be effectively used.

In thoughts and words, the bearer of the type can reproach both specific people and society as a whole when he does not find an opportunity to realize himself, to reveal his abilities, that his life is not filled with meaning, that it is not clear what his resources and potential opportunities are spent on. This is a signal for help that the carrier of the type sends to the surrounding space.

This signal can also take other forms, for example, it can look like an indirect, and sometimes direct, complaint, or as demonstratively meaningless behavior, when a person is looking for a way to “kill time”. The content of such signals depends on the function and can look like, as an expectation of a hint regarding what exactly to do and what not to do, what values ​​to focus on, how to relate to a particular event or phenomenon.

You can help a person with this function if you offer him a suitable resource. However, here you need to be careful not to become a victim of obsessive attachment. The easiest way to get such help is from a dual. The individual tries to optimize the use of funds to metabolize, but it is difficult to do it on his own, and therefore he develops a subconscious expectation of help from the outside. If such help does not come, the carrier of the type remains in the dark about how to approach the problem of self-realization, since the person's psychosomatic system remains "de-energized". The defeat of this function makes a person indiscriminate.

According to the Suggestive and Role functions, a person feels subconscious desire to learn and improve one's skills, and learning itself in this case is not only not a burden but is perceived as a very natural and necessary process, turning into a source of inspiration and hope. Ausra says, that a person’s feelings here are “as if crumpled”, and it is almost impossible to sort out this lump without outside help. Each person here needs support in structuring the aspect corresponding to his type. Someone needs help to sort out relationships, and someone with emotions; to some - with their abilities, to others - with their consumption, etc. Support and advice in this case are accepted with gratitude and immediately put to work.

People who can help with the “necessary” aspect are sympathetic. According to this function, a person subconsciously expects interest in communication from a partner and is surprised and disappointed when he does not meet the expected response.

The acquired knowledge, sometimes with the naivety of a child, is implemented in their everyday life and at work.

**Motivational-Mobilization (Mobilizing)**: Vital, inert, productive, situational, verbal, potential, objective, passive, activation.

Being inert, it accumulates information related to its aspect and constantly preserves the formed or forming tendency.

This function collects information specific to it, without showing any activity, and needs a needed source (to the Suggestive) that awakens enthusiasm and high energy tone.

If the carrier of the type gets into a situation that requires from him at least some initiative in terms of to this function, he feels “out of place”, is shy and looks embarrassed. In the absence of the necessary information on this function, a person can aimlessly or as if in oblivion walk back and forth or sit motionless. If the function receives unfavorable support from the family or work colleagues or some “necessary” person, then, as Ausra writes, “he demonstrates his bad mood without the slightest remorse”. In fact, this is a signal sent to the surrounding space with a call for help. But in this case, the “right” help can only come from the dual or activator.

The productivity of this function is expressed in that it forms an emotional response according to the IME. Being inertial, it “gets stuck” on the formed response, preserving it until it receives a new portion of energy-informational feeding. Its functional semantics is based on aspect Fe*.

(*Translator’s note: Churyumov was an ILE.  He contends that the pattern of information metabolism within ILE applies to all types.)

Ausra, while working on her model, called this function differently - activation, waiting for mercy, regulatory, but always emphasized that according to this function, a person shows extreme insecurity, is afraid of reproach, reacts painfully to critical remarks, is not able to express her needs in words, waits for specific help. Ausra says that the Mobilizing is a “window through which you can enter each person and buy his soul ...”. According to this function, a person, under no circumstances, shows independence, strictly fulfills what is expected of him, what conditions they create for him with their feelings” and “can only be the way he is programmed” by others. If a person receives adequate support for this function, his subjective (i.e., characterized by the Demonstrative) productivity increases sharply, and his mood becomes optimistic and combative, when he feels he has the strength to cope with any task related to his competence. A person's behavior for this function is similar to behavior during intense love, when the lover idealizes the object of love and is ready to make almost unlimited sacrifices for him, identifying with the beloved.

According to this function, a reproach that the bearer of the type could address to his environment is supposed, but not brought to verbal form. The meaning of this reproach is that the bearer of the type is not appreciated, his virtues are not seen, and also that he is not loved as he should be. Defeat of this function affects a person's ability to love.

**General description of Super-Id:**

SUPERID is a source of vital activity, is the energy basis of any productive activity, and in this sense, can be called a "psychomotor block" (Ausra). The success of the SUPERID block itself almost entirely depends on the living environment in its objective or subjective manifestation, which is determined by the information content of this block. This block determines a person's well-being, depending on the satisfaction of needs, his readiness for active activity and inspiration, which is the result of the sublimation of excess energy.

According to SUPERID, as under hypnosis, complete mental identification of one person with another can occur. A leader who has caught the wave of the SUPERID crowd is able to control it as an extension of his own body.

It is difficult to consciously tune in to your own SUPERID, but if you manage to do this, then the body becomes accessible to conscious control, when, for example, overcoming bad habits becomes a solvable work task.

Although a person is not aware of his SUPERID, but the subconscious attitude requires not to show weakness in this block. Theoretically, this can be explained by the fact that the strength or weakness of this block depends on external support, and even if and he is weak, then, it means, the person does not deserve more. And since he does not deserve it objectively, then there is nothing to complain about, because not only will help not come, but the misunderstanding may only intensify and will be openly indicated. An indirect complaint, as a signal of trouble, must find a suitable addressee, otherwise there will be no reaction to it or it will be inadequate to the request.

The SUPERID as a mental organ can be used to assess the immediate environment. "The SUPERID tries to understand what value the world has for him, how it pays for the individual's participation in the SEM (social-energetic metabolism)". If the state of the SUPERID is bad, then this should be understood that the immediate environment is also objectively harmful to the person to a corresponding extent. However, he may not be aware of this and, by inertia, will not go to change it, getting more and more bogged down in it, and, thus, reducing his already not very high chances. Ausra quite rightly called this block the anti-conscience block, and this is also one of her remarkable discoveries. A person must take care of himself and count on support from others, at least to be a useful member of society. "...if an individual, thanks to dualization, is aware of his needs, he can really take care of the needs of others, without violating his own interests. We can say that the individual treats the world the way the world treated and treats him."

Ausra says that "To betray is to ridicule according to SUPERID". A very constructive and meaningful definition.

Primary social imprinting is carried out through SUPERID, and this can also be considered a variant of suggestion. The well-known cases of infants, when they, by coincidence, grew up among wolves, sheep, or dogs, can, from a socionic point of view, be understood as "loading" the SUPERID of these children with socio-biological programs alien to their human nature. If a person's SUPERID does not contain programs for a specific activity, then when it is necessary to engage in such an activity, the person becomes disoriented and will feel like Robinson on a desert island, when he must start from scratch. Unfortunately, in this case this means that he will have to go through the entire evolutionary path, and this is impossible for an individual. When a person must respond to reproaches or comments from others that he acts the way he can, this means that we are dealing with a projection of the SUPERID archetype. The difference between optimal and real behavior that exists in such cases is explained by the fact that the person was not trained in SUPERID, did not receive adequate information on this block in time. It is safe to say that without understanding his SUPERID, a person cannot claim emotional and cultural maturity. Without receiving the appropriate information on SUPERID, a person is unable to objectively assess his place in the world and his relations with it. In this case, objectivity means acceptability from a social point of view. An adequately programmed SUPERID turns a person into a full-fledged citizen, capable of not only harmoniously being present in it, but also taking part in its creative transformation. In this case, a person's demands on the world become adequate to the demands that the world makes on a person.

Various deviations in the development of SUPERID are manifested in inadequate socialization, altered sexual orientation, delayed emotional and cultural maturity. If a child does not receive enough parental love in childhood, primarily maternal love, then this should be considered as a rather severe defeat of his personal sphere, and this will be expressed in various anomalies in family and civil life. Understanding the cause of such anomalies, it will be possible to undertake targeted personal correction. A full-fledged sense of humor cannot be formed without the full participation of SUPERID. It can also be assumed that congenital damage to SUPERID manifests itself in severe forms of dementia, up to debility.

If a person makes a mistake in the SUPERID block, then he remains confident that he was “set up”, and with a pure heart reproaches others and shifts responsibility to them. He can repeat this mistake again and again if he is not provided with emotional and informational cover from the environment. Considering the readiness of SUPERID to accept information adequate to its content, flows, it can be assessed as a suggestive entry into the psyche of a person. The concept of expectation can also be associated with the SUPERID block, which is understood as a subconscious expectation of certain actions from the environment. It is expected that these actions will be of a resource-providing nature.

In the absence of support from people who can provide the necessary resource, the carrier of the type switches to the "minimal existence" mode, which is characterized by decreased well-being, minimal productivity, creative passivity, and loss of vitality. Thus, it can be said that according to this function, a person expects a resource to be provided to him, and he expects this as if he had some sovereign right to it. This situation is not simply reminiscent of, and in fact, in its deep meaning, is not simply analogous, but identical to the situation when a baby is demanding to be fed with breast milk, and no one disputes this right. SUPERID is a social entrance to the human psyche, and this also means the possibility of manipulating him. However, we emphasize that manipulation is a socially pathological form of relationship, which is opposed to cooperation and actualization, that is, interested and benevolent support of the individual, aimed at developing his best abilities.

**ID:**

**Imperative-temporal (Ignoring)**: Vital, inert, accepting, situational, laboratory, programmatic, relative.

It is called passive by Ausra simply because it is in the vital, or psychosomatic, ring. Here passivity should be understood as an automatic reflection of generalized processes occurring in the mental, or intellectual-operational ring, where the environment is modeled, goals adequate to it are developed, decisions are made and volitional impulses are formed, which are transmitted to the vital ring. The Ignoring function can be called passive because it automatically reflects the informational state of the Base function together with the behavior programs formed on it. In addition, according to this function, a person does not choose anything independently - here he is completely dependent on the environment and receives all impulses from others.

Having received such an impulse, a person feels obliged to work it out, but he does this only when the source of the impulse is assessed by him as worthy, deserving respect. However, this function, regardless of its position in the vital ring, is distinguished by maximum activity since it is responsible for the implementation of the personality's programs into life. Literally speaking, we can say that this function passively, that is, automatically, immerses the personality in activity.

The semantics of this function is based on the concept of time*, contact with which is imperative for everyone, and personal programs and their implementation determine the internal scale and counting of time. This IME reflects the topics on which a person mainly spends his time.

(*Translator’s note: Churyumov was an ILE.  He contends that the pattern of information metabolism within ILE applies to all types.)

To implement its programs, the individual must spend some time, but it has no choice here, since the formed program automatically immerses the individual in the process of its implementation, also automatically allocating the necessary time resource to perform the corresponding work.

The inertia of this function is expressed in the fact that the subject of its IME is distinguished by stability and constancy. A person according to this function is not inclined to change the object of its application. It is this property that can explain why, for example, extroverted ethicists are constantly immersed in relationships, and introverted ones - in emotions, etc.

The combination of such properties as inertia and acceptance is manifested in the fact that this function accumulates information and fixates on it, and this is expressed in the extreme concentration on the projections of the archetype.

This function imperatively adapts and subconsciously adjusts to the corresponding values ​​of a partner and a social group, feels that it has no right to impose its ideas on others. This function subconsciously assesses the degree of reasonableness with which other people build their behavior.  It acutely experiences deviations from this criterion as its own imperfection and immediately offer its help and abilities, so that the partner could improve their performance. A person uses his own resource for this function to compensate for a lack of resources in the other, even when not asked to do so (inertia).  In case of compatibility, such behavior is accepted with varying degrees of gratitude and yields positive results. If the degree of compatibility with the partner leaves much to be desired, then the attempt to "help" does not achieve success and ends in mutual dissatisfaction, up to and including conflict and breakup. The components of behavior for this function are usually beyond awareness, and the person acts automatically. At the same time, the person feels the theme of the partner's behavior for this aspect quite specifically, voluminously and distinctly, and what the suitable partner does seems important, essential and primary. In such a case, one wants to support one's partner, to meet him halfway, which in some cases (with compatibility) may look like increased compliance, compliance and understanding, and in others (incompatibility) - like obsession, inappropriateness and simply immodesty.

In the case of pathological deviations, a person here is unable to concentrate on the topic of the aspect or, on the contrary, it becomes an obsession for him.

Due to the automatism of aspect adjustment according to this function, the bearer of the type perceives other people's manifestations according to this function more realistically than his own. Moreover, he seems to meet the aspect manifestations according to this function of another person, showing understanding and readiness to support him according to this aspect. From the outside, this may look like increased compliance, even weakness, but, by nature, this is a manifestation of the natural ability to selflessly participate in the manifestations of others in this aspect.

**Implementation-technological (Demonstrative)**: Vital, contact, productive, evaluative, laboratory, program, object.

Its primary semantics is associated with the direct performance of physical work (Te*). This is a passive, automatic receipt of a product. Here, the paradox is that the concept of passivity is combined with an obvious need to act. But here, activity is separated from initiative, this is the automatic activity of a programmed robot. Of course, a person is not a robot. This is a spiritual being, endowed with free will, but these qualities are fully manifested in the Base and Creative. Here we can only talk about the extremely precise execution of programs formed in another place. Thus, an impulse aimed at obtaining a specific result is formed (presumably) in the brain, but the movements of the executive organs, for example, the hands, are apparently strictly adequate to such an impulse.

(*Translator’s note: Churyumov was an ILE.  He contends that the pattern of information metabolism within ILE applies to all types.)

Although adequacy is only an ideal, which can be approached by the coordinated work of the organ that forms the image of the result, and the executive organ that materializes this image.

Firstly, a high level of coordination here, if it is not innate, as, for example, in the case of a baby sucking on its mother's breast, is achieved because of the practical use of the executive organ, and in this case, there is no limit to perfection. Excellent examples of this can be numerous examples of mastery and virtuosity demonstrated by people in various spheres of work, science, art and public life. However, in many cases it is possible to see how imperfect the work of the executive body is, even though, apparently, the image is fully formed. How clumsy, for example, can be the movements of a person's fingers trying to thread a needle.

Ausra writes that "According to the Demonstrative, the potential energy of an individual in any work activity is realized." According to this function, a person acts as an instrument of technological transformation of a certain component of the living environment, and his work itself can be considered as a specific technology.

The definition of this function as demonstrative or demonstrational, found in socionics literature, is only partially justified - in the sense of what a person is capable of, but not in the sense that he shows off in front of other people for ambitious or advertising reasons. However, if there are people in your immediate environment who can appreciate, support, and fairly treat the work being done, this becomes an additional incentive to continue it. Ausra writes that “By his actions, the individual demonstrates his attitude to the program of society laid down in the previous Ignoring function.” However, here the concept of demonstration obviously does not contain a shade of “show-off”, but is synonymous with the concept of “expressing, demonstrating an attitude " and, thus, give feedback to the environment, and, as Ausra writes, "This attitude is always positive." The presence of interested witnesses sharply increases the working tone and productivity of the type carrier.

If a person does work on the aspect of Demonstrative, he never gets tired, that is, he works on this IME until he falls down, but at the same time he does not feel tired, but only limited by ability to continue to work - move arms and legs. Concentration on this function can reach such a level that a person looks like he is obsessed, and those who are not obsessed with this subject or, at least, are not interested in it, the carrier of the type simply does not pay attention, and they cease to exist for him. According to this function, the individual never competes - he simply does everything he is capable of.

The work of this function ensures the materialization of that ultimate socially demanded result, which, according to its typological characteristics, the carrier of the socionic type. According to this function, a person can produce a socially valuable and typologically colored product, but for this he must receive adequate stimulation according to the mobilization function. As a result, he must develop the conviction that his work is needed by other people, and it is done for them. Demonstrative, like Creative, needs positive reinforcement, which can be expressed in a fair reward, tactfully expressed praise or compliment, as well as an interested and inspiring look from a partner.

Depending on the IME that is in the position of this function, the individual demonstrates the maximum creative abilities available to him.

The optimal sphere of activity for a person is determined by the aspectual filling of his Demonstrative, and not by his Base. Base is a tool with which a person “works with the world,” but one produces their maximum product with Demonstrative. IEE and SEE have different Base, but their optimal product is filling the environment with a powerful emotional charge.  ILE discovers the laws of nature, which become the basis for new technologies. The SLE also create technologies, but these are technologies of military victories.

Pathological deviations in the development of Demonstrative are manifested in a decrease in productivity and in the inability to complete the work started, and as a result – in social inability or inadequacy. If at a particular moment the EGO is for some reason unloaded, passive, demoralized or pathologically changed, then the Demonstrative is activated, which can manifest itself in meaningless actions.

**General description of Id:**

It seems that the ID in socionics is understood narrower than in Freud's psychoanalysis. For Freud, it is an endless ocean of uncontrolled impulses. In socionics, the ID is a psychosomatic reflection of the EGO, a bodily materialization of programs formed with the direct participation of the intellect. The participation of the intellect here does not mean that the formation of programs is a completely conscious process. Moreover, the work of the intellect is largely uncontrolled by consciousness and is not realized, although here much depends on the definitions of intelligence. The socionic interpretation of ID makes it possible to assume that ID is not realized because the information associated with it is represented in the psyche in completely different codes than those used by consciousness. This is because in the socionic ID mechanisms of transformation into codes accessible to waking consciousness are not represented. New information about the world.

The socionics ID can be understood as a substructure of the psyche responsible for the materialization of EGO programs. In computer terminology, it can be compared to a driver that makes programs "visible" to peripheral devices. From the point of view of the computer metaphor, the existence of such a driver is quite justified, although options for its software implementation are possible. There are signs of the functioning of the ID that an external observer can see. First, these are all behavioral acts with their psychological assessment, and, in addition, these are emotional states and reactions. Whatever a person does, it is always a transformation of behavior programs into behavior itself.

The socionic model of the psyche allowed Ausra to discover the intentional and motivational aspects of the ID. The ID is capable of fully functioning only in the presence of external motivation, that is, it "turns on" only when it is stimulated by the environment. In the structure of the psyche, the environment is represented by the SUPERID. EGO creates new values, the need for which has matured in society, and ID strictly depends on the values ​​existing in the environment. According to this block, a person imperatively recognizes the rights of society, a group or even a partner to himself and experiences negative tension if these instances do not sufficiently use the rights granted to him. This feature of ID makes the connections between the individual and his environment very strong. This block acts as a mental organ, with the help of which a person learns, or rather feels his value, which is an integral condition for the fullness of life. This organ gives a person the opportunity to grasp his place in social processes. Ausra expressed all this as "The more society needs me, the more it needs my services." Thus, an individual can do what he does because society needs it, because there is an explicit or implicit social order.

By realizing his ID, a person guarantees himself support from society, a group or a partner, and thus the satisfaction of his needs.

All this, in the case of normal development and functioning of the ID, makes it practically impossible for an individual to fall out of society and resist it.

In this sense, even cases of extreme asceticism and hermetism can be understood not at all as a withdrawal from society, but as an attempt to solve a very important problem for society, which the individual perceives as his own.

This block makes a person accessible to education.

A person without ID can be compared to a paralytic who is unable to do anything, or even to make any meaningful sounds. Therefore, it can be said that thanks to this subsystem of the psyche, a person is able to master and transform the surrounding world. Of course, one can also imagine a situation when a person uses his executive organs only to test and demonstrate his capabilities to others or to himself, but this does not contradict the instrumental nature of ID, and such situations themselves can be considered as preparatory or calibrating. The same is true for training situations, in which the product is a new level of abilities.

When implementing this block, a person not only demonstrates his maximum capabilities, and therefore, in this respect, can serve as an example to follow. But he has an acute, although unconscious, need to confirm his usefulness to society as feedback, and, consequently, the right to receive the corresponding life resource. These expectations could be described by the words "Look how good I am!" In the performance of Demonstrative, such a statement is a sincere statement of the fact of high-quality work and has nothing to do with bragging.

If a person makes a mistake in the ID block, he reacts sharply to the incident, openly expresses dissatisfaction not only with himself, but also with his environment, which did not protect him from the mistake, did not warn him, did not intervene. Furthermore, he tries to consider the acquired experience, but this happens at an unconscious level and is expressed as an action of acquired automatism.

ILE:

SUPEREGO (SeFi) (resistance):

 "The number of units of force pressure (Se) per unit of critical attitude (Fi)". This can be understood as follows: in tense situations, the individual decisively overcomes or discards formal ethical (Fi) standards (Se) and creates new ones. This attitude can be characterized as confrontation, resistance, or alienation.

SUPER-ID (SiFe) (expectation):      

The individual expects the environment to receive the maximum amount of life resources.  The results of such expectation are recorded here by emotional reactions.  For a certain number of units of resource, the individual responds with one unit of emotional activity. Such an attitude can be characterized as expectation or identification.

ID (NiTe) (concentration):

The individual is imperatively focused on performing work. Time is imperative - it does not wait, is not reversible, is an absolute value, and if someone does nothing, he simply loses time and the corresponding resource. Work is the main means by which a vital resource is created. Thus, Id is a mental function that directly corresponds to physiological tone and determines its level necessary to ensure life. Such an attitude can be characterized as concentration or readiness.

SEI:

EGO (SiFe) (self-affirmation): the number of units of resource, well-being per one unit of emotional response.  Comfort is maximized.  Strives to get more life resource for each emotional reaction. Consumption acquires a dominant character.

SUPER-EGO (NiTe) (resistance): The amount of time per one unit of productivity. The time during which one unit of physical labor can be performed is maximized. At the level of everyday life, the person performs physical work slowly, spending a lot of time on each unit of physical work, which means that its physical productivity will be low.  Only doing physical work (Te) when absolutely necessary.  But devotes maximum time communicating with people (Fe).

SUPER-ID (NeTi) (expectation): The number of potential opportunities per one communicative unit. Shows an increased interest in everything related to the meaning of life, and in each act of communication tries to get as many units of such meaning as possible.  Strives for contact with partners who can fill his life with meaning.

ID: (SeFi) (concentration): The number of units of volitional effort per unit of intertype relationship. Directs all its will to creating and maintaining relationships with other people. Can establish contacts relatively easily.

ESE:

EGO (FeSi) (self-affirmation): The number of units of emotional response per unit of life resource. As emotional response is maximized, the maximum number of units of emotionality is issued per unit of well-being, and this is ensured by the type structure - it can afford it.  In response to minimal resource support from the partner, the individual responds with such a powerful emotional reaction of joy or gratitude that it not only compensates for the partner's resource expenditures, but also significantly covers them. This creates a precedent for further resource support. Here the emotional component of life is maximized. The possible maximum of emotional energy is allocated for any unit of consumption or life resource. If the partner does not have enough such energy, then he has a reason to try, since in such contact he receives evidence of his need, which is one of the projections of self-affirmation. Emotional response acquires a dominant character.

SUPER-EGO (TeNi) (resistance): The number of units of productivity per one unit of time. Maximizes productivity under conditions of increased environmental pressures.  Can increase the production of vital resources in extreme conditions, thereby increases his chances of survival. 

SUPER-ID (TiNe) (expectation): The number of communicative units per one unit of potential opportunities. In search of a source of meaning in life tries to establish as many contacts as possible. This program leads to the individual exhibiting increased social activity, thereby filling his life with the meaning it lacks.

ID (FiSe) (concentration): The number of intertype relationships per unit of force pressure. The individual concentrates on interpersonal relations with an emphasis on volitional dominance.  Strives for self-affirmation by concentrating power in his hands, which can be expressed in material wealth.

**CHAPTER 4**
